proof.claim:
Going backwards must be possible, deliberate, and audited — never accidental.

WHY THIS EXISTS. On 2026-08-16 a bad controller shipped and the rollback was
REFUSED:

    desired-state: refusing to regress cluster-controller — desired floor is
    1.2.317, attempted 1.2.316; pass --allow-regression to override (audited)

That refusal is correct behaviour and it was still a surprise, at the worst
possible moment, on a degraded cluster. "Can I get back?" is the only question
that matters once something bad is running, and nothing in the suite answered
it. An operator should learn how the guard behaves from a test, not from an
incident.

THE TWO PROPERTIES, and they pull against each other:

  1. A regression must not happen by accident. `services desired set` to an
     older version is refused unless the operator explicitly asks, so a
     mistyped version or a stale script cannot walk the cluster backwards.

  2. A regression must remain POSSIBLE. A guard with no override is not a
     safety feature, it is a trap: it converts "we shipped a bad version" into
     "we shipped a bad version and cannot leave". The override exists, is
     explicit, and is audited.

WHAT THIS SCENARIO CAN AND CANNOT DO HERE. Exercising the floor needs two
published versions of one package, and a release bundle ships exactly one
version per package — so on a freshly built simulation the older artifact
simply does not exist to roll back to. What IS reachable, and is asserted
here, is that the control plane refuses to move desired state to a version it
cannot resolve, and that a refusal leaves no residue behind.

The full floor test belongs on a cluster that has taken at least two releases
of the same package. That is the real cluster, and it is the reason this
scenario states its limit rather than quietly asserting less than its name
claims — a scenario whose name overpromises is how a suite loses its meaning.

authority.note: Simulation output is evidence/candidate knowledge only. Governed promotion is required before production may rely on it.
